Resolves #21993

The Gantt Cancel and Save test now waits for the editor's App Worker mount flight before targeting its buttons. The two Escape cases keep their original path.

Evidence: L3 headless Chromium on the real Gantt example → L3 required.

Micro-review eligible: mechanical — one existing browser spec waits for the boundary it acts on.

CI jobs: +0.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | The pointer test checks the same Cancel and Save focus return after the real editor reports mounted, visible and no mount flight. |
| AC-2 | The two Escape cases retain their input and assertions. |
| AC-3 | Outside CI, the three cases passed all 36 executions in a 12-repeat Chromium run. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The spec owns the readiness boundary for these pointer assertions.

## Test Evidence

With the example data from the failed hosted job, I repeated the contested input order three times in headless Chromium. During the opening transition, a trusted pointer-down went to Cancel and pointer-up at the same coordinates went to a field label. The editor stayed open. A new click after the mount flight settled closed it and restored focus to the task each time. The patched spec passed 36/36 on the branch base. `git diff --check` and commit hooks passed.

### `@neo-opus-ada` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-22T17:57:44Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical, test-only. One spec gains a readiness wait in front of two pointer interactions; no product code changes.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The claim is that the pointer case raced the editor's opening flight: Cancel was pressed while the dialog still moved. The fix waits until the real editor reports mounted, visible and `mountFlight === null`.
- `mountFlight` is the engine's own boundary. `Component.mjs` sets it for a mount attempt and clears it when the attempt settles (`src/component/Base.mjs:2045`), and `Dialog`'s animated show checks it (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:1157`).
- The predicate is the same one `webdesktop/Apps.spec.mjs` and `webdesktop/PhoneAndTouch.spec.mjs` already use, so it adds no new idiom.
- `gantt/basic` runs dedicated workers, so `page.workers()` finds the App Worker.
- Both Escape cases are untouched (AC-2).
- At `9614d2d4f0` all 7 required checks are green, and my own 3-repeat run passed 9 of 9. That sits beside your 36 of 36 for AC-3.

I looked for a wait that could mask a product defect, for example focus restoration skipped when the flight never settles. Instead, the poll fails with its own message if the editor never finishes opening, and the focus assertions after each click are unchanged.

**Findings:** None.
